- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust upward slightly.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- If forecast is below 75% of recent 18-day low, consider upward bias correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid sharp upward moves unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.4) and recent price is trending up.
- If sentiment is flat (0.0) and forecast is volatile, assume mean reversion; smooth out extremes.
